extracted.intended_audience: book reviewers for Springer Nature (academic/publisher reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for conducting peer review of books submitted to a commercial academic publisher, covering responsibilities, conflicts of interest, institutional restrictions, confidentiality, and alignment with COPE ethics. Intended to direct how reviewers should evaluate, disclose, and handle submitted works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must ensure 'consistent ... review of material sent for review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evaluations that are consistent across submissions to allow fair comparison and editorial decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must ensure 'fair ... review of material sent for review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bias and treat authors and their work impartially; do not allow personal views or relationships to unduly influence the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must ensure 'timely review of material sent for review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return reports within agreed deadlines so editorial decisions and publication timelines are not delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose qualification concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should disclose any 'qualifications concerns' that may affect their ability to assess the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack expertise in parts of the manuscript or otherwise feel unqualified, inform the editor so an appropriate reviewer can be sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide honest, constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should provide 'honest feedback' while avoiding 'unfair negative comments, personal or unjustified criticism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on evidence-based critique, point out strengths and weaknesses, and offer suggestions for improvement rather than ad hominem or unsupported denigration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure — financial
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must reveal potential financial biases such as 'grants, stocks, consultation fees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any financial relationships that could reasonably be seen to affect impartiality so editors can decide whether you should review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure — non-financial
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must reveal potential non-financial biases including 'professional relationships, advisory positions, mentoring connections.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose relationships, personal or professional, that could create a perceived or real conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional restriction on reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers cannot assess works from authors or editors at their current institution, with limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept review requests for submissions involving colleagues at your current employer unless the publisher explicitly approves (exceptions may exist for very large institutions or niche fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent mentoring or collaboration disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must disclose recent mentoring or collaboration relationships within three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have mentored, collaborated with, or had a close professional relationship with an author or editor within the past three years, disclose this to the editor as it may preclude reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of manuscript content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must not 'reveal details of the Work such as data, information, interpretation, discussion or review reports' without author and publisher permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat manuscript materials as confidential: do not share, cite, or discuss them outside the editorial process unless explicitly permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on repurposing unpublished material
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers cannot repurpose unreported material for their own research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, data, methods, or other privileged information seen during review for your own publications, grant applications, or projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to COPE reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature aligns with the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), whose peer reviewer guidelines apply to book reviewers as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE's ethical standards and recommendations for reviewer conduct (e.g., conflicts, confidentiality, integrity) in addition to publisher-specific rules.
